data.content: Using TESTED_FOR_TOXICITY relationships (`tox_value_mg_L`) and measured concentrations (MEASURED_AT), which substances have the smallest margin between measured levels and toxicity values (i.e., highest implied risk), and does this align with them being labeled drivers (IS_DRIVER)?

args.query:
Identify the highest implied risk exposures by comparing measured concentrations to species-specific toxicity values.

For each substance s with a measured concentration at a site-time (relationship (s)-[m:MEASURED_AT]->(st)), join to all available toxicity tests (s)-[t:TESTED_FOR_TOXICITY]->(sp) with t.tox_value_mg_L. 
- Use the measured median concentration m.median_concentration_mg_L and require it > 0 (detected).
- Compute TU_by_species = m.median_concentration_mg_L / t.tox_value_mg_L for each species sp.
- For each substance–site-time pair (s, st), keep the species that yields the maximum TU (TU_max) and record that species.
Return the top 20 substance–site-time records with the highest TU_max, including:
  s.name AS substance,
  s.cas AS cas,
  st.site_name AS site,
  st.country AS country,
  st.year AS year,
  st.quarter AS quarter,
  sp.name AS species_max_TU,
  TU_max,
  m.median_concentration_mg_L AS conc_mg_L,
  t.tox_value_mg_L AS tox_value_mg_L_at_max,
  EXISTS( (s)-[:IS_DRIVER]->(st) ) AS is_driver
Order by TU_max DESC
Limit 20.

data.content:
Here’s what I found by comparing detected median concentrations (MEASURED_AT) with species-specific toxicity values (TESTED_FOR_TOXICITY), computing toxic units (TU = concentration/tox_value_mg_L) per species and keeping the maximum TU per substance–site–time. The highest TUs represent the smallest safety margin (highest implied risk).

Top results (showing 5 of the top 20 highest TU_max)
| substance     | cas         | site     | country     | year | quarter | species_max_TU | TU_max  | conc_mg_L | tox_value_mg_L_at_max | is_driver |
|---------------|-------------|----------|-------------|------|---------|----------------|---------|-----------|-----------------------|-----------|
| Deltamethrin  | 52918-63-5  | n34      | Sweden      | 2009 | 3       | crustacean     | 1283.09 | 0.0950    | 0.00007404            | true      |
| Deltamethrin  | 52918-63-5  | 11wvo001 | Netherlands | 2011 | 4       | crustacean     | 877.90  | 0.0650    | 0.00007404            | false     |
| tau-Fluvalinate | 102851-06-9 | 11wvo001 | Netherlands | 2011 | 4       | crustacean     | 858.43  | 0.0650    | 0.00007572            | false     |
| Bifenthrin    | 82657-04-3  | 11wvo001 | Netherlands | 2011 | 4       | crustacean     | 677.44  | 0.0650    | 0.00009595            | false     |
| Cyfluthrin    | 68359-37-5  | 11wvo001 | Netherlands | 2011 | 4       | crustacean     | 626.20  | 0.0650    | 0.0001038             | false     |

Does this align with IS_DRIVER labels?
- Observation from the top 20: 8 of 20 highest TU_max cases are labeled as drivers (IS_DRIVER = true), while 12 of 20 are not.
- Notably, the single highest TU_max (Deltamethrin, Sweden, 2009 Q3) is labeled as a driver, but several other very high TU_max cases (including the next four listed) are not.
- Species perspective: 18 of the top 20 maximum TUs come from crustacean toxicity endpoints.
- Sites/countries: 14 of 20 occur in the Netherlands, with 10 of 20 at site 11wvo001.

Interpretation (grounded in the query results):
- Alignment is mixed. Some of the highest implied risk instances are labeled as drivers, but a majority of the top-20 are not.

Reproducibility: run this Cypher to get the full top-20 list
```
MATCH (s:Substance)-[m:MEASURED_AT]->(st:Site)
MATCH (s)-[t:TESTED_FOR_TOXICITY]->(sp:Species)
WHERE m.median_concentration > 0
  AND m.concentration_unit =~ '(?i)mg/?l'
  AND t.tox_value_mg_L IS NOT NULL AND t.tox_value_mg_L > 0
WITH s, st, m, sp, t, (m.median_concentration / t.tox_value_mg_L) AS TU_by_species
ORDER BY TU_by_species DESC
WITH s, st, m, collect({species: sp.name, tox_value_mg_L: t.tox_value_mg_L, TU: TU_by_species}) AS tuples
WITH s, st, m, tuples[0] AS top
RETURN
  s.Name AS substance,
  s.casrn AS cas,
  st.name AS site,
  st.country AS country,
  m.year AS year,
  m.quarter AS quarter,
  top.species AS species_max_TU,
  top.TU AS TU_max,
  m.median_concentration AS conc_mg_L,
  top.tox_value_mg_L AS tox_value_mg_L_at_max,
  EXISTS((s)-[:IS_DRIVER]->(st)) AS is_driver
ORDER BY TU_max DESC
LIMIT 20
```

Access the full Neo4j graph (and run the query on the complete dataset) via the dockerized database on Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/14616124

If you want, I can list all 20 entries or filter by species, site, or time window.
